candidate_relations.reason: The clinical picture is driven by highly elevated serum complement-fixation IgG titers (1:512) and CSF complement-fixation titers (1:8) for Coccidioides, along with pulmonary nodular consolidation and lymphadenopathy consistent with coccidioidomycosis. The reference diagnosis is Coccidioides meningitis with pseudo-SAH appearance. Neurocysticercosis is a different parasitic etiology (Taenia solium) and, while it can cause subarachnoid disease in a Central American immigrant, it does not account for the Coccidioides serologic findings, the pulmonary findings, or the pseudo-SAH pattern described. These are distinct diagnostic entities.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: Neurocysticercosis (subarachnoid) vs. Coccidioides meningitis presenting as pseudo-subarachnoid hemorrhage

case_quality_flags: Highly specific serologic evidence (serum CF IgG 1:512, CSF CF IgG 1:8) strongly supports Coccidioides meningitis; pseudo-SAH on CT is a recognized but uncommon presentation of this entity
Immigrant from Guatemala traveling through Mexico places patient in Coccidioides-endemic corridor (southwestern US/Mexico)
